primitives.name: Remainderless Distribution Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: IN ECONOMIC THEORY 19 distributive shares other than profit, we may express the same principle by saying that the tendency is toward a remainderless distribution of products among the agencies contributing to their production.
primitives.assumptions: Perfect information and zero transaction costs imply remainderless allocation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When transaction costs exceed marginal benefit, remainder emerges.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian allocation model mirrors theoretical remainderless distribution via posterior belief updates on agency contributions.
layer2.telemetry: Distribution efficiency ratio measuring deviation from ideal allocation.

primitives.name: Cost-Value Divergence
primitives.verbatim_quote: But in actual society, cost and value only "tend" to equality; it is only by an occasional accident that they are precisely equal in fact; they are usually separated by a margin of "profit," positive or negative.
primitives.assumptions: Market imperfections cause persistent divergence between cost and value.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Equilibrium occurs when Δ = 0; otherwise, profit persists.

layer2.mapping: GSE state transition engine uses Δ as feedback signal to adjust market equilibrium states.
layer2.telemetry: Profit margin variance across time series indicates market stability.

primitives.name: Risk-Uncertainty Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: The key to the whole tangle will be found to lie in the notion of risk or uncertainty and the ambiguities concealed therein.
primitives.assumptions: Risk is quantifiable; uncertainty is not, leading to conceptual confusion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Confusion arises when R and U are conflated in decision-making models.

layer2.mapping: GSI probabilistic inference framework separates measurable risk from irreducible uncertainty in profit forecasting.
layer2.telemetry: Entropy-based measure of decision ambiguity in strategic planning.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight centers on the distinction between theoretical remainderless distribution and practical cost-value divergence. In perfect competition, all productive inputs receive proportional share, implying no surplus. However, real-world markets exhibit persistent profit margins due to imperfect information and transaction costs. This discrepancy leads to the fundamental problem of profit, which is reframed as a contrast between idealized and actual competition. The resolution hinges on separating risk—measurable uncertainty—from true uncertainty—irreducible randomness. These dualities create epistemic failure modes where misclassification of uncertainty leads to flawed profit models. Mathematical formalization requires probabilistic frameworks that distinguish between stochastic risk and aleatory uncertainty, enabling robust inference in GSI and adaptive state transitions in GSE.
